critical_code_review_comments: iter90b.py reissue endpoint: when old_id == new_agr['id'] (unlikely), the artist_profiles.agreement_id + reissued_at/by fields are NOT updated (both writes are inside the `if old_id and old_id != new_agr['id']` branch). If _generate_agreement is deterministic on inputs and produces same id, the audit trail is silently skipped. Consider always updating reissued_at/by even if id matches, or asserting new id != old id.

iter90b.py manager_chat_threads: unread_count uses `read_by: {$ne: user['id']}` — matches messages missing the user's id in read_by array. This will include the manager's own outgoing messages if their sender_id isn't auto-added to read_by on send. Verify that /chat send handler pushes sender to read_by.

iter90b.py threads sort: sort() with reverse=False on tuple ( -unread_count, created_at ) — since unread is negated, ascending gives higher unread first (correct), but created_at ascending puts oldest first when unread is equal. Doc says 'unread first' + 'last-message-desc'; the created_at comparison should be reversed.
